An agent working in a split has no dock row anywhere (#2024). #2019 built the indented sub-entry, then reverted it after the active-row highlight failed four separate times.The four faults, from the recovered post-mortem: (1) the sub-entry hardcoded active: false (b5f0bdc58); (2) the fix read focus through the seeding accessor, so asking darkened the parent row (1ea67bc33); (3) the fix for that made parent and split mutually exclusive, breaking the parent-keyed e2e contract (0f550d896 fixed it); (4) the fix for that set data-active with no CSS listening (baf4bf8bf fixed it). All four passed a green unit suite. The faults were not four accidents: each was a different way of mis-assembling a fact the client never stores — which terminal has the keyboard. The server already treats a split as a full terminal (an optional parentId packages/padi/src/vocab.ts); the client demotes it to chrome of its parent, storing its focus parent-relatively (focusTarget: "main" | "sub" + activeSubTab in useSubPanel), so every surface must join two stores to answer the question — and each join is a fresh chance to get it wrong.The join is spelled today in useTerminalStore.focusedId(), in TerminalContent’s pane resolution, and (before the revert) in useFocusedTerminal — three spellings of one question. Note also a correction to #2024: it says peekSubPanel was “kept”; it was not — the revert removed it.

The plan: store the answer once, derive everything else, then re-land the sub-entry. Equal as data, subordinate on screen — hierarchy survives only as placement (parentId) and presentation (indentation, no Cmd+N of its own).Peer rows stay rejected per #2024: flattening would break the one-to-one mapping between top-level rows and Cmd+N shortcuts.

The fact and its folds

One per-host signal, focusedTerminalId: TerminalId | null, valid for any terminal — split or top-level. It is written only by verbs (focusTerminal(id), collapsePanel(parent)), and everything the four faults mis-assembled becomes a derivation:The implementation keeps exactly one written value, { id, tileHint }, and exposes focusedTerminalId() as its public projection. tileHint bridges only the create-RPC → retained-metadata gap, preventing the active tile from flickering to a not-yet-published split; live placement always wins as soon as it arrives, so later re-parenting remains honest.

  • The active tile is a fold, not a second fact: activeTileId = topLevelOf(focused) via parentId. Parent row and sub-entry can never fight — the tile fact is defined as the ancestor of the focus fact, so “both lit when you type in a split” holds by construction, and fault 3 becomes a contradiction in terms.Deriving in this direction (focus written, tile folded) rather than the reverse keeps exactly one written fact. The reverse — tile written, focus in a side store — is today’s model, and the join is the bug factory. Deriving also keeps re-parenting honest for free: setTerminalParent and restore’s promoteOrphanedRestoreChildren change parentId, and a memo follows; a stored tile id would go stale.
  • useSubPanel shrinks to genuine chrome: collapsed, panelSize, the remembered tab, rememberedPane, refocusNonce. focusTarget is deleted; “is focus in this panel” is parentOf(focused()) === id. rememberedPane is written and read only by focus verbs: it lets a landing choose main or the remembered visible split, but no derivation or memo may consult it. That verb-only path is why this is landing chrome rather than focusTarget returning as a second focus authority.
  • The landing walk collapses: today reaching a split takes four writes across two stores packages/client/src/canvas/dock/useDockFocus.ts; focusTerminal(id) becomes one write plus write-through of remembered chrome. useDockFocus keeps its interface and loses its body.
  • The wire is untouched: chrome.setActive still reports the derived tile; only collapsed/panelSize persist, as today. Restore focuses the persisted top-level terminal.

Solid reactivity rules

The model only stays sound if the reactive discipline is explicit — each rule below is one of the four faults made unspellable:

  1. Reads are pure. Derivations (createMemo) may never touch an accessor that seeds state. The seeding getSubPanel is deleted outright: verbs call ensureState internally, reads get a peek-only face — so fault 2’s whole category (a read that writes, inside a memo) is gone.The hazard was live until FX1: useTerminalStore.focusedId() and TerminalContent both read through the seeding accessor. It happened to be inert (a fresh seed had activeSubTab: null), but FX1 removed the landmine, not just the current trip-wire.
  2. Side effects live in verbs, never in effects watching derived state. Visit-MRU, unread-clearing, and the setActive report happen inside focusTerminal. A createEffect on activeTileId would re-fire on restore seeding and on transient metadata gaps; a verb fires exactly when the user acts, so a momentarily-wrong memo (e.g. parentId not yet streamed during restore) is inert.While metadata for the focused id is absent, topLevelOf returns the id itself and the memo corrects when parentId arrives — safe only because nothing effectful watches it.
  3. Row predicates are createSelectors. isFocused and isActiveTile wrap the two folds, so a focus move updates the two affected rows instead of re-running an equality in every row of the dock.createSelector subscribes each key individually: a change notifies the old and new key only — O(2) — where activeId() === row.id in N rows is N comparisons per move. With sub-entries the dock’s row count grows, so this stops being theoretical.
  4. Edge-triggered stays imperative. refocusNonce survives as-is: “re-grab the keyboard with an unchanged value” is an edge, not a level, and reactive state cannot express it. Everything level-shaped goes through the fact.

FX1 — one focus fact

FX1· one focus fact✓ shipped
blocks → FX2 · FX3links #2043

Introduce focusedTerminalId beside the activation choke point in createViewState; fold activeId from it; delete focusTarget, the seeding accessor, and the four-step walk; route useTerminalStore.focusedId(), TerminalContent’s pane resolution, and useDockFocus through the fact.

User-facing change: none — that is the point. Anything that looks different is a bug in the phase.

To test the PR: exercise every focus surface and confirm nothing moved. Open two terminals, give one a split; click between main pane, split pane, and the other tile — the dock highlight, the pane dimming, and where your keys land must behave exactly as on master. Then the edges: collapse the panel (keyboard returns to main), close a sub-tab by its ✕ (keyboard re-grabs), Ctrl+Tab / Cmd+1..9 / Cmd+F, and a reload (same tile focused, panel state restored).

Done when: focusTarget and getSubPanel no longer exist in the client; useDockFocus is a single focusTerminal call; the six focusedTerminal.test.ts fold cases and the useSubPanel.test.ts transition cases pass against the new derivation; and the existing e2e contracts pass unmodified — the parent-keyed active row, the exact-"" assertion, the [data-focused] world contract.The contracts: dock.feature “Active terminal carries a visible indicator”, terminal-switcher.feature:23 (asserts data-active === ""), sub-terminal.feature’s count steps, world.ts’s [data-focused] .xterm-screen. Green-with-edits is not the gate; green-untouched is — the phase exists to prove the fact re-plumb changes no behaviour.

FX2 — the sub-entry, re-landed

FX2· dock sub-entries▶ do next
needs ← FX1links #2024

First commit: recover dockRowActive.test.tsx from the reverted diff and adapt it to the fact — the render-level state matrix is the only test in this story that lived where the bugs did.Recovery: git fetch origin refs/pull/2019/head; the test is whole in baf4bf8bf, SubAgentRow.tsx’s final form in 4ed6fc809, the revert is 7a3d7edef. The matrix: never-opened split, focus in main, focus in the split (both lit), sibling split focused, collapsed, different tile, no tile. Then the feature: every split earns an indented sub-entry under its parent’s row — agent or plain shell.This widens #2024, which argued agent-only rows; the owner overrode that on 2026-07-29: all sub-terminals show in the dock. An agentless split renders label + landing only — no state pip, no attention wash (it has no agent to speak for). The row component spreads dockRowAttrs (which derives data-active internally for splits via isFocused — no parameter to hardcode) and lands via focusTerminal(id); section headers still count only split agents, through the same urgency fold the host tab already uses; sub-entries share their parent’s activity-window fate. With splits enumerated, the ⊟ N sub-count chip is redundant and is removed (SubCountChip, data-sub-count, and their e2e steps).Deliberate waiver: the “existing e2e unmodified” gate is lifted for exactly the chip assertions in sub-terminal.feature / sub_terminal_steps.ts, which are replaced by sub-entry assertions. Every other existing assertion — the parent-keyed active row above all — remains untouchable.

User-facing change: every split has a home in the dock — an indented entry under its host terminal’s row (agents wear their pip and attention wash there; a plain shell split is just a labeled row). Clicking one lands you in that pane, keyboard and all. The ⊟ N chip is gone — the rows themselves are the count. Repo section headers still count split agents, so the header agrees with the host tab above it.

To test the PR: split a terminal (Ctrl+Shift+`) — an indented row appears under the parent’s dock row immediately, plain bash and all, and the ⊟ N chip is gone. Run claude in the split and give it a task: the entry gains the working pip. Click the sub-entry: you land typing in that pane, and both the parent row and the sub-entry are highlighted. Let the agent block on a question: the sub-entry washes violet and the section header’s count matches the host tab’s.

Done when: the recovered matrix is green; a new e2e scenario asserts an agentless split’s row exists (and no ⊟ chip anywhere); another types into a split and asserts the parent row and the sub-entry both carry data-active; a repo section header’s count equals its host tab’s; and the sub-entry renders as a direct child of .dock-cards-section.The active-highlight and wash rules are scoped with a direct-child combinator (.dock-cards-section > [data-dock-row]); a sub-entry nested in a wrapper element silently exits every rule — fault 4 by another door. Direct-child placement is therefore a gate, not a style choice.
